summary: Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory (~1867–1872), the University of Jena (~1874–1881), and Heidelberg University (~1881–1882), and held a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Rashmi Yadav is an Indologist who studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra (M.Sc., 2016–2018), Chaudhary Charan Singh University (2020), and Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University (Ph.D. student, 2022). She joined Chaudhary Charan Singh University's Faculty of Vedic Mathematics in 2021.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Fergusson College under Ramchandra Dattatraya Ranade and Dr Bhune, and guided by Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinvijaya, he was professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930) and president of Gujarati Sahitya Parishad (1964).

Rasmus Nyerup (1759–1829) was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Copenhagen (~1777–1784). He served at the Royal Danish Library (1784–1803) and was Chief Librarian at the University of Copenhagen (1796–1829).

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, he held several posts at Copenhagen, including librarian, professor of literary history, and chair of Oriental Languages.

Ratna Basu is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. Attested in 2026, she has served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society.

Ratna Handurukande is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Harold Walter Bailey. She held lecturer positions at the University of Ceylon, attested in the Department of Sanskrit in 1970, and at the University of Peradeniya.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga as his traditional teacher and succeeded him in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming the Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

Ravi Prakash Arya (born 1961), an Indologist educated at Panjab University, served in Haryana's Department of Higher Education (1993–2019). He later directed the Indian Foundation for Vedic Science (2019–2021) and served as Chair Professor at Maharshi Dayanand University (2021–2025).

Ravindra Singh Bisht (born 1944) is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Lucknow, Kumaun University, and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology. He held posts in Haryana and Punjab archaeology departments and was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1983–2004).

Ravindra Suryakant Kale is a scholar in Indology and computational fields. He held library posts at IOCL, Mahila Mahavidyalaya, Prof. V. B. Shah Institute of Management, and Narmada College of Management, before becoming Librarian at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University in 2014.

Ravinjay Kuckreja is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied theology and religious studies at the University of Chester (2014–2017), marketing at IE University (2017–2018), and completed a doctorate in religious studies at Universitas Hindu Negeri I Gusti Bagus Sugriwa (2020–2023).

Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and physics. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University, later serving as a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University.

Ray Caldwell Smith (1872–1922) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the San Francisco Theological Seminary (~1897–1900) and later held a post at the Landour Community Centre Language School.

Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Galway and under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1886–1892), and Reader at the University of Cambridge (1901–1907).

Raymonde Linossier (1897–1930) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. She studied under Sylvain Lévi (~1920–1930) and held an unsalaried attachée post at the Guimet Museum in 1925.

Reb Anderson (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar and practitioner. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded, serving as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.

Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk and worked as a lector for Tibetan Studies at the University of Hamburg.

Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Washington and Yale University, later holding posts as Associate of Law at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and Professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
